# Endpoint notifications keep pool threads out of single-threaded apartments

Source: crates.io `cpal` 0.18.2, upstream commit `e1612d5d98152f8dc2a62e1b51ef7cbf4f7f26b7` in <https://github.com/RustAudio/cpal>. Original registry archive SHA-256: `6f02e8d0327b42d3e2e4ab2119af397344eb9fc54a34bf0ddeaa1277af8681f1`. Retains the upstream manifest, `Cargo.toml.orig`, `.cargo_vcs_info.json`, README, build script, examples and Apache-2.0 license. The upstream crate lockfile and repository-only files are omitted; the workspace Cargo.lock controls resolution.

Problem ([RustAudio/cpal#1402](https://github.com/RustAudio/cpal/issues/1402)): a default-device stream registers an `IMMNotificationClient`. When an endpoint is removed or becomes unavailable (a monitor's audio sleeping, a headset unplugged), `OnDeviceRemoved` and `OnDeviceStateChanged` look up the current default through `com_initialized`, which calls `CoInitializeEx(COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED)` on the Windows thread-pool thread that runs the callback. That thread stays a single-threaded apartment for good. `ActivateAudioInterfaceAsync` does its work on the same pool, and whenever it lands on such a thread it fails with `RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE` (0x80010106). In Leech this broke system audio for screen shares ("ActivateAudioInterfaceAsync (0x80010106)") until restart. A test that left 64 pool threads single-threaded reproduced the failure on every attempt for over 600 ms, whatever apartment the activating thread used.

Change: `src/host/wasapi/device.rs` adds `default_endpoint_exists`, which joins the multithreaded apartment only for the lookup, releases the endpoint and balances `CoUninitialize`. A thread that already has an apartment keeps it. `src/host/wasapi/stream.rs` uses it in those two callbacks, and its test `serein_tests::notification_callbacks_leave_the_thread_apartment_alone` calls both callbacks and then checks that the thread can still join the multithreaded apartment. The test fails with `RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE` on unpatched 0.18.2. Both modified files say so in their first line. Nothing else changes; cpal's own threads still initialize as before.

Validation: cpal's dev-dependencies are not part of this workspace, so remove the `[dev-dependencies.*]` sections from this manifest temporarily and run `cargo test --offline -p cpal --lib serein`, then restore the manifest. The test needs the Windows audio service. It does not prove which threads Windows uses for endpoint notifications; that they are pool threads is the upstream report's finding, consistent with the reproduction above.

Remove this patch when a cpal release fixes #1402 (for example via [RustAudio/cpal#1413](https://github.com/RustAudio/cpal/pull/1413), open on 2026-11-02).
